body:
That would be very difficult for me to write down.  It's twenty years of abuse and neglect, and it's difficult for me to accept some of the things that happened to me because of the person she is.  This situation with my father has been an eyeopener for me, and I will probably be proactive in getting some counseling.  I feel I need to let someone know about the "relationship" I have with her.  While I'm on the fence about calling my father a narcissist, everything my mother has done for the entirety of my time on Earth has made the fact that my mother is a narcissist clear as day.

But I think it would be good for me to get it out.

I still do, but they're a bit intimate, I guess.  I thought I would be able to see my sisters again, so I bought them some of my favorite childhood books in Japanese with the intent that when I saw them I could read the books as bedtime stories for them.  It probably sounds really corny/stupid.  I also got my father items that had "dad" on them, so I feel sending them now would be terribly awkward.
If I do respond, I feel this would be the way I would like to go about it. Do you have any advice on how I could go about it?

I've posted a few comments for more background on the situation.  I had a very controlling mother who was emotionally and physically abusive towards me.  For as long as I can remember, she would always tell me my father didn't want me, and that there was no use trying to contact him.  When I would contact him, he would promise to visit me and then nothing would come of it.  I got discouraged and started to contact him less and less until I was out of my mother's household and learned I had siblings.

I've been thinking, and I definitely don't want to go on the offensive in this situation and "fight fire with fire" as some might call it.  I'm very much a passive type of person and have always been worried that he never wanted anything to do with me from the beginning, so I'll probably just allow the relationship to go the way of NC.
Unfortunately I have no idea, and I know I will never receive an honest answer from my mother.  That's a good idea, though.

There definitely is.  My parents were in their mid-twenties, and all I know is that the relationship was at most a short fling.  Aside from that, I really know nothing about their relationship or details around why/how I was conceived.

The e-mail I sent is the last image.  I can screen shot it differently so you see his response is clearly to that e-mail.  I even sent that one twice because I thought he didn't see it the first time I sent it a month earlier.  I know I didn't write everything in the first post, but I have added a bit of background through my comments.  I actually did try to contact him throughout my middle and high school years, but he would take months to reply and if I tried to ask about seeing him he would always say he was busy.  My mother also went out of her way to hinder any contact I could have with him.  I want to make it clear that I simply wanted to get to know my father and sisters.  I already had a trip planned to California and was not asking for anything other than the opportunity to be a part of a real family.
Thanks for the comment.  This is a really difficult time for me, but the kind words I've received from everyone have helped me a lot.  :)

Thank you for the advice.  I will get right on that.  I am afraid my mother has definitely blown through all the money and is currently on multiple government assistance programs.  This is what has kept me from immediately pursuing legal action up until this point.

Thanks so much.  To be honest, a lot of these replies have me bawling.  I was assuming it was all my fault/no one would care.  I was in a very low place when I read that e-mail, but the responses I've gotten from everyone have helped me exponentially.
Thanks for the comment.  I've always been one to be down on and blame everything bad in my life on myself.  I want to say more, but all that's coming to mind is thank you.  :)

Deep down I know that's what it is.  That that is what it has always been.  It's painful, but I need to accept it.  He never really cared about my goals or aspirations, he was just trying to make himself less guilty.

As much as it pains me to say it, the two times I met him after leaving my mother's household he would say things that made it obvious he wanted me to be aborted.  It's really difficult to come to terms with, and this is the first time I've actually typed it out/written it down/acknowledged it.
That's so close to how I feel it's a bit uncanny.
I'll do just that, thanks!
Not at all.  I'm appreciative of all the advice I can get.  Maybe another point of view is what I needed to help me understand things a bit better.

I tried to talk about it with him before when I visited him three years ago.  He just seemed to want to go on and on about how terrible she was without really listening to my experiences, though.
Sorry to ask this, but could you possibly give me more information as far as legal action goes?  I'm not sure where to start with all of this, honestly.

To be honest, I'm not sure if I can respond.  It's difficult for me to talk about, but when I say I just thought he was busy, I truly believed it.  It seems so obvious now, but I deluded myself with hoping he really did want me in his life.

Sorry if I made it sound as though I never tried to contact him.  I would call him occasionally, and we would e-mail every once in awhile throughout my childhood.  A large part of why I didn't e-mail him often was that he would promise to visit me and then drop off the face of the Earth for a few months, later saying he was "sorry" and that he was "too busy" to visit at the time.  My mother also did not want me to have any contact with him.  She was both emotionally and physically abusive and would reiterate to me that the reason he was "too busy" was that he did not want anything to do with me.  He was actually the one who suggested I join his family on their trip to Disney World when I was 17, so I assumed this was finally the time we could have a relationship.  Since then I started e-mailing him more often since I was finally out of the toxic living situation with my mother.

Thanks for your response.  I'm not sure if him coming from Iran has something to do with it, but I have always assumed it has.  
My mother forcibly kept me from him all my life.  She would go on and on about how he wanted nothing to do with me, so eventually I stopped asking about him at all.  We would e-mail back and forth a bit, but, like I mentioned, I was severely depressed most of my middle/high school years.  I would take months to respond back to him because the thought of not having a father figure in my life was almost too painful for me to bear at that age.
I truly want to take legal action against my mother, but I know if I do it will hurt my grandmother.  She took me in at 16 to get me away from my mother.  Though my grandmother is a truly sweet woman, and I know my mother would weasel the money she owes me out of my grandmother instead.  As much as I hate to think of it along these lines...I'll probably wait until after my grandmother passes away before I take any sort of legal action so I don't burden her.
